$comment: Measured off clay_0/clay_4 (side: sole stack, cuff hang, throat wall),
clay_5 (back: cuff wings, and how close the two cuffs come to touching),
clay_2 + body_2 (front: lace run, toe cap, lateral overhang) and body_0
(textured side: which parts are brass and which are sole).  Panel heights
were converted with the alpha bbox and meta.height = 1.72.
ROUND 3.  Everything below marked R3 was re-read with a per-row run
decomposition of the panel (out/boots_probe.py) rather than by eye off a
grid, and measured against the same decomposition of the render
(out/boots_raw.py, which reads a --frame 1.80 preview in its own metric
frame).  Two structural corrections came out of it.
R3-A  THE POSE.  skel.ankleL is 47 mm above and 28 mm in front of
skel.ankleR.  place() used to translate y by a literal 0, so both
boots stood on the world floor and the stagger vanished.  On clay_2
the bottom 47 mm of the figure is ONE run -- her right boot alone,
0.103 m wide at y = 0.02 and 0.114 at 0.04 -- and the left boot only
joins in at y = 0.047.  The render had two boots there, merging into
one 0.31 m run at yaw 315 against the sheet's 0.11.
R3-B  THE CUFF IS WIDEST AT THE FOLD, NOT AT THE HEM.  Following the
planted boot's own axis on clay_2 (x = -0.060 at y = 0.20 drifting to
y = 0.20   run -0.123..+0.061   outer reach 0.063   the hem
y = 0.30   run -0.146..+0.126   outer reach 0.091   the fold
so laterally the collar GROWS on the way up.  Fore and aft clay_0
says the opposite -- 0.230 deep at y = 0.195 against 0.178 at 0.295.
Both earlier versions had the lateral relation inverted and flared
the collar down and out into a bell, which is the pancake the review
measured.  foldHalf* and rimHalf* are now two separate superellipse
outlines instead of one plus an anisotropic interpolation weight.
SIDE VIEW.  The panel is orthographic, so panel-x IS world z; the union of
the two boots covers z in [c*zMin - s*halfW, c*zMax + s*halfW] with
c = cos(footToeOut) = 0.9895, s = sin = 0.1445.  Run widths off clay_0,
against the same rows of the render (R3):

so the boot was 11-18 % too long fore-and-aft through the whole foot and
the same again through the cuff.  toeZ 0.150 -> 0.138 and heelZ -0.070 ->
-0.062 take 20 mm out of the footprint (0.220 -> 0.200 local length), which
is 19.8 mm off the projected side view.  R3.
DEPTH AT THE ANKLE.  The one row the two side panels agree on: at y = 0.14
clay_0 reads 0.187 and clay_4 0.198, at 0.16 they read 0.171 and 0.170, and
the render was 0.230 / 0.204 -- 19 % deep in both.  shaftDepth 1.35 -> 1.22,
-0.0025 -> 0 (the cords were standing 2.5 mm PROUD of the throat, and at
yaw 90 it is the lacing, not the leather, that sets the front edge) take that
FRONT AND BACK, ACROSS.  Per-boot run widths at the boot's OWN local
height (clay_2 y, and clay_5 y, each less that boot's own lift), meaned
over the four readings the two panels give -- the near boot is inflated by
perspective in both, by up to 40 %, so neither panel alone is a target:
local y   clay_2 planted / lifted   clay_5 planted / lifted   mean   render(r2)
The shaft was already right and the FOOT was 20 % narrow: the reference's
boot is a compact block, widest across the ball at 0.122 and tapering to
0.091 at the ankle, where the render was a flat 0.096 all the way up.  With
the projected width = 2*halfW*c + L*s, 0.122 wants halfW = 0.050 at the
ball, measured back off the render rather than solved: soleHalfW 0.041 ->
0.042 (0.047 over the welt) and upperHalfW 0.039 -> 0.050, with the waist
and the heel behind the ball pulled in 6 mm so only the ball bulges.  R3.

WHAT THE PANELS WILL NOT AGREE ON.  A boot 0.20 long and 0.09 wide cannot
project narrower than about 0.19 at 45 degrees off its own axis, yet clay_1
and clay_3 both read the boot at 0.10-0.11 in the bottom 0.08 m -- the same
width clay_2 reads dead ahead.  The two side panels disagree with each
other the same way: clay_0 shows the two boots almost coincident (0.239
total at y = 0.04) and clay_4 shows them 0.15 m apart fore-and-aft (0.361).
The turnaround is a perspective sheet whose intermediate panels are not at
45 degrees and whose camera pitch varies, so the three-quarter boot widths
are not a reachable target for an orthographic render at a pinned yaw.
What IS reachable there, and what round 3 goes after, is the run STRUCTURE:
one boot at the floor rather than two, and a boot mass that carries up to
y = 0.33 instead of stopping at 0.29.
Local frame: authored around the ankle's ground projection with +z toward
the toe, then yawed by pose.footToeOut and dropped onto skel.ankle{L,R} at
that ankle's own height.
